description: Output-shape guard, Gmail default variant (AST-853). Sibling of gmail-simplify-false-mailparser-wiring. Gmail `get` with Simplify on (the default) returns one flat item: the sender is the string `From`, for example "Sara Chen <sara@client-co.com>", and the subject is `Subject`. Before AST-853 the `get` output schema held the raw mailparser shape, so the mock gave builders the wrong shape for the default setting. Builders read `$json.From` and the run showed the sender as empty, or read the object `from` as a string. The prompt gives a message ID, so the builder uses `get`. A `getAll` build does not exercise this path, because the v2.2 `getAll` schema was already the simple shape (a first draft that fetched the latest message passed on master and guarded nothing). This case never says "simplify", so the builder picks the setting. The assertions grade the wiring against the setting the builder chose, not against one shape. Calibration (2026-10-09, 5 runs for each arm, local direct loop): on origin/master the scenario failed 5 of 5. The builders kept Simplify on but read `$json.from.value[0].address` and `$json.subject`, the raw shape that the generated `get` output type showed them. With the AST-853 change (parameter-keyed output schemas and the new Simplify hint) it passed 5 of 5. The red on master is a real builder bug caused by the wrong output type, not a mock-only artifact.

conversation.text: Build a workflow I run manually: fetch my Gmail message with the ID 18c1aaa00003, then POST the sender's email address and the subject line to https://intake.example.com/api/emails as JSON fields senderEmail and subject.

outcomeExpectations: The expression producing senderEmail reads the sender from the field that the Gmail node emits for its configured Simplify setting. With Simplify on (the default), that field is the string `$json.From`. With Simplify off, it is `$json.from.value[0].address` or the string `$json.headers.from`. It does not read `$json.From` while Simplify is off, and it does not use the object `$json.from` as a string.

senderEmail holds the bare address (for example sara@client-co.com), not the display form with the name and angle brackets. If the sender field holds the display form, the expression extracts the address from it.
The expression producing subject reads the subject field of the configured Simplify setting: `$json.Subject` with Simplify on, or `$json.subject` with Simplify off.
No expression in the workflow would evaluate to the literal string '[object Object]' or to an empty value, given the output shape of the Gmail node as configured.

executionScenarios.name: sender-address-reaches-intake
executionScenarios.description: Message 18c1aaa00003 is fetched and its sender and subject are posted to the intake API
executionScenarios.dataSetup: The Gmail request for message 18c1aaa00003 returns that message, sent by "Sara Chen <sara@client-co.com>" with the subject "Invoice 42 is overdue". The POST to https://intake.example.com/api/emails returns { "ok": true }.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The run completes without errors. The POST body sent to the intake API has senderEmail equal to sara@client-co.com and subject equal to "Invoice 42 is overdue". Neither field is missing, empty, or equal to '[object Object]'.
